clue.text: Thick Indian laughs

parts.note: the Inca were the native people of the Andean empire, so an Indian of Peru
hoots are loud bursts of laughter

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person of Indian origin is mocked with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' looks like a slur on the Indian, but it is the definition in its sense of close or intimate, as in 'thick as thieves'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thick with someone is to be very friendly or conspiring together, which is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Given another order, managed to enter block

indicators.note: the two short words are put in another order, the last moved to the front

parts.note: got in means managed to enter

explanation.surface: After a new instruction, somebody managed to get into the building block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given another order' swaps GOT IN round, moving IN to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, typically gold or silver.

clue.text: Lever second set of seats into vehicle

indicators.note: the row goes into the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
in a theatre, the second row is row B

explanation.surface: Someone levers a second row of seats into a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is an iron bar used as a lever for prising things open.

clue.text: Extremely happy chap in charge, likely to boom

indicators.note: the extreme letters of happy, its first and last

parts.note: a chap is a person

explanation.surface: A very cheerful man in charge has a loud voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes H and Y, the outer letters of 'happy', not 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypersonic aircraft travel far beyond the speed of sound and so generate a sonic boom.

clue.text: Last in series after a long time, and a brief one, are up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the pieces read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an age is a very long time
a mo is a moment, a brief time

explanation.surface: The final episode arrives after a long wait and a brief one, and they are over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are up' turns both time words round together, as this is a down light; 'after' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so the last in that series.

clue.text: Beg sailors to welcome N European officer

indicators.note: the beggar and sailors take in, or welcome, the European

parts.note: to sue is to plead or beg
a Balt is a person from the Baltic states in northern Europe
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with sailors to welcome a Northern European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to welcome' has the beggar-plus-sailors pair take the northern European in, just after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British Army a subaltern is a junior commissioned officer below captain.

clue.text: Here's the doctor —— that's a relief

definitions.text: Here's the doctor —— that's a relief

parts.words: Here's the doctor —— that's a relief
parts.note: read as a sigh of relief when the physician turns up, but a relief is also a stand-in, so this is a doctor covering for another

explanation.surface: A worried patient sighs with relief as the doctor finally arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in physician is literally the relief for the regular doctor, covering the practice temporarily.

clue.text: Attached to line, medal's rounded part

indicators.note: the medal is attached to the end of the line letter

parts.note: OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour, worn as a medal

explanation.surface: A line has a medal's curved section attached to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobe is a rounded projecting part, as of the ear or a leaf.

clue.text: Missionary, in middle of crossword, having soft drink brought round

indicators.note: the drink is brought round the other piece, containing it

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: only the middle letters of the synonym are kept, its outer two at each end dropped

parts.note: read as cross word, an angry complaint: a grumble

explanation.surface: A missionary, halfway through a crossword, has a soft drink brought to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossword' is read as 'cross word', GRUMBLE; 'middle of' keeps UMB, which COLA surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: St Columba was the Irish monk who brought Christianity to Scotland from Iona.

clue.text: Minute horse is among weird collection of animals

indicators.note: the horse is placed among the letters for weird

parts.note: eerie means strange and weird
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A tiny horse lives among a strange collection of creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of wild animals kept for exhibition.

clue.text: Keen fan's endless sorrow about publisher

indicators.note: the shortened sorrow goes round the publisher, standing about it
the synonym for sorrow loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: grief is deep sorrow
OUP is Oxford University Press, a well-known publisher

explanation.surface: An eager follower is grieving over a publishing house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the sorrow word and 'about' wraps it round the publisher. The 's is a link standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows a band around adoringly is a devoted, keen fan of it.

clue.text: Tiny capital teacher lost in wicked city …

parts.note: baby can mean very small, as in baby carrots

indicators.note: the teacher is lost from the capital, so those letters drop out

parts.note: London is the capital of the UK
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A small-capital teacher went missing in a city of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes DON from LONDON, leaving LON. The ellipsis runs this clue into the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Mesopotamian capital is a biblical byword for a city of luxury and vice.

clue.text: … place to worship Baal, centre being redeveloped

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds something in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the wicked city: a shrine to the god Baal whose centre is being rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being redeveloped' rearranges BAAL and CENTRE. 'centre' looks like part of a building being rebuilt, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a tent or building used as a sanctuary, so a place of worship.

clue.text: Pollution finally chokes cat

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of chokes

parts.note: mog is British informal slang for a cat

explanation.surface: Polluted air ends up choking the cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes S, the last letter of 'chokes'. MOG (also moggy) is everyday British slang for a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Smog is a mixture of smoke and fog, a familiar form of urban air pollution.

clue.text: In the afternoon, holding comparatively poor classes in such art?

annotationWithheld.why: In the afternoon, holding comparatively poor classes in such art? (10): POST + N (after noon) round MODER fits, but no reading of 'comparatively poor classes' gives MODER, and no blog parse was found
annotationWithheld.clue: In the afternoon, holding comparatively poor classes in such art?

clue.text: Freight initially halved in value in slow passage

indicators.note: the opening letter is the Roman hundred, which halved in value becomes the Roman fifty

parts.note: cargo is freight carried by ship or plane

explanation.surface: Freight loses half its value at the start of a sluggish run.
explanation.walkthrough: The C at the start of CARGO is the Roman numeral 100; halving it gives 50, the numeral L.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a very slow tempo, and a movement played so is a slow passage.

clue.text: Gladstone for one almost elevating rubbish he delivers

indicators.note: almost loses the final letter

parts.note: Gladstone was a Liberal Prime Minister of Victorian Britain

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevating lifts the word so it reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Gladstone was nearly lifting rubbish that he delivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts LIBERAL to LIBERA; 'elevating' turns ROT into TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberator sets people free, that is, delivers them from oppression.

clue.text: Publicity about route as devised for old flyer

indicators.note: the publicity letters stand about the rearranged route

parts.note: PR is public relations, that is, publicity

indicators.note: something devised is worked out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A publicity campaign plans a route for an aged pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' looks like part of the surface's planning, but it signals the rearrangement of 'route as'; 'about' has the publicity letters surround the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The pterosaurs were winged reptiles of the dinosaur era, so prehistoric creatures that flew.

clue.text: Irish saint shortly filled with love raised appeal for his country

indicators.note: the shortened saint is filled with the other pieces
shortly cuts the final letter

parts.note: St Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: it is sex appeal, as in the 1920s 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A shortened Irish saint, full of love, makes a rousing appeal for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the saint's last letter; 'raised' turns the appeal word upwards; 'filled with' puts love plus that turned word inside the trimmed saint, before its final C.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriotic person acts out of love for his own country.

clue.text: Paperwork a heavy burden on British sport

indicators.note: the paperwork and burden come on, that is after, the letter for British

parts.note: admin is administrative paperwork
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: Bureaucracy is a heavy load on British sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Cleaning light cover

definitions.meaning: the act of wiping off dust from furniture
a thin layer, as of snow or sugar

explanation.surface: Cleaning a light fitting's cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Housework wiping away dust has this name, as does a light sprinkling that covers a surface.

clue.text: Sample thank-you note son inscribed

indicators.note: the son is written into the middle of the other two pieces

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A little thank-you card is signed by a son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inscribed' writes the son's letter between the thank-you and the note, like a name on a card.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste food is to try a small amount of it, which is to sample it.

clue.text: Fruit and nut, alas, is off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The fruit and nut chocolate has gone bad, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is off' rearranges NUT and ALAS; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a dried seedless grape, a dried fruit used in baking.

clue.text: Wine was being promoted

definitions.meaning: a pink wine made with brief skin contact, written with an accent in French
past tense of rise: went up in rank

explanation.surface: Someone drank wine while being promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Pink wine carries this name, and the same letters are the past tense of rise, meaning went up.

clue.text: Can girl go out with low neckline?

indicators.note: going out with the letters sends them off into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Can a girl go out on a date wearing a low-cut top?
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out' rearranges CAN, GIRL and LOW; 'with' is a link. The question mark admits the definition is loose: this is a collar, not a low neckline.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing collar is a stiff stand-up shirt collar with turned-down points, worn round the neck with formal dress.

clue.text: 20 green sheep

parts.note: green means go, as in traffic lights
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Twenty green sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 20 across, read as the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Got up means rose, as from bed, which is the answer to the cross-referenced clue.

clue.text: Irritated food shop owner finally turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of owner

explanation.surface: A deli owner was annoyed when finally arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses DELI + R as a whole, giving RILED.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means annoyed or angered, so irritated.

clue.text: Crazy about English fermented drink

indicators.note: the mad letters go about, round, the English letter

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: The English are crazy about their brewed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink made by fermenting honey and water.

clue.text: From spear, superficial damage after brief stumble

indicators.note: the damage is placed after the shortened stumble
brief shortens the word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: a trip is a stumble
a dent is surface damage, as to a car

explanation.surface: A spear only causes a dent after a quick stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts TRIP to TRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, as carried by Neptune.

clue.text: Woman plunged into work that's afoot

indicators.note: the woman is plunged into the middle of the word for work

parts.note: toil is hard work
Ena is a woman's name, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A woman throws herself into some job that is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' looks like 'in progress', but the definition means 'something that is on a foot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A toenail grows on the toe, so it is literally something found on the foot.

clue.text: Inflexible and unresponsive? That's not feminine

indicators.note: the feminine letter is not there, so it is taken away

parts.note: frigid means cold and unresponsive
F is the abbreviation for feminine in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone stiff and cold is being described as unwomanly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff and unbending, so unable to flex.

clue.text: Seeking favour as EU policy's being dealt with

parts.note: CAP is the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Union
in hand means being attended to

explanation.surface: A farm policy is being sorted out to win support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To go cap in hand is to ask humbly for something, as a supplicant seeking favour.
